title: Kernels and cokernels of ind-constructible sheaves
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. The two coefficients below mean the canonical condensed rings $\underline E$ and $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$, pulled back to $X$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the internal module category of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], constructibles of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and the replete small-filtered-colimit closure $\operatorname{IndCons}$ of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness].

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ and $f\colon B\to B'$ a morphism in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Let $P_f$ be the
category of commutative squares consisting of a map $v\colon C\to D$ in $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ and maps
$C\to B$, $D\to B'$ compatible with $f$. Then $P_f$ is filtered, the projections $P_f\to J(B)$ and
$P_f\to J(B')$ are cofinal, $f=\varinjlim_{P_f}v$, and

$$
\ker f=\varinjlim_{P_f}\ker v,\qquad\coker f=\varinjlim_{P_f}\coker v
$$

lie in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$.

Here $P_f$ is essentially small; its colimits are taken over a small skeleton, as for $J(B)$ in [det-ind-heart-canonical-presentation]. The displayed colimit identifications are those induced by the squares: the arrow cocone has legs $(C\to B,D\to B')$, the kernel cocone has the induced maps $\ker v\to\ker f$, and the cokernel cocone has the induced maps $\operatorname{coker}v\to\operatorname{coker}f$.

proof.text: Use the existing Grothendieck abelian instance for internal modules, lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck, specialized to the canonical pulled-back coefficient. It supplies the ambient abelian structure and small exact filtered colimits.

source.place: Final paragraph: exactness of filtered colimits in the ambient module category

proof.text: The closure theorem gives an abelian constructible category whose inclusion preserves finite colimits, and the smallness theorem gives essential smallness. Map arrows preserves finite colimits componentwise. Thus the costructured arrow category has finite colimits and is filtered (IsFiltered.of_hasFiniteColimits). Essential smallness follows by passing Arrow to the small constructible model and the Mathlib smallness instance for CostructuredArrow.

source.place: First paragraph: finite colimits of squares

proof.text: Source cofinality, directly. Let $S:P_f\to J(B)$ be the source projection. For $j=(C_0,c_0)$ put $L(j)=(C_0,C_0,1,c_0,fc_0)$. On a morphism $a:j\to j_1$, define $L(a)=(a,a)$; the equations over $B$ and $B'$ verify that this is a functor. An object of $(j\downarrow S)$ is $p=(C,D,v,c,d)$ together with $u:C_0\to C$ satisfying $cu=c_0$. There is a unique morphism from $(L(j),1)$ to it: the pair $(u,vu)$. Its target compatibility is $dvu=fcu=fc_0$, and uniqueness follows from the identity top arrow of $L(j)$. Hence every such comma category has an initial object; any two objects are connected by the two arrows from that object, so it is nonempty and connected. This proves cofinality in its comma-category sense, without a finite-presentation or later-stage equality argument.

source.place: Second paragraph: cofinality of the source projection; explicit identity-square argument replacing choices of lifts

proof.text: Target cofinality, directly. Let $T:P_f\to J(B')$ be the target projection. For $j'=(D_0,d_0)$ put $R(j')=(0,D_0,0,0,d_0)$. On a morphism $b:j'\to j'_1$, define $R(b)=(1_0,b)$; these pairs preserve identities and composition. An object of $(j'\downarrow T)$ is $p=(C,D,v,c,d)$ together with $u:D_0\to D$ satisfying $du=d_0$. The pair $(0,u)$ is the unique morphism from $(R(j'),1)$ to that object. Thus this comma category has an initial object and is nonempty; any two objects are connected by the two arrows from that object. This proves target cofinality.

source.place: Third paragraph: cofinality of the target projection

proof.text: Identify the colimit arrow, including its cocone maps. By [det-ind-heart-canonical-presentation], the tautological diagrams on $J(B)$ and $J(B')$ have colimits $B$ and $B'$. Here is the reindexing argument explicitly, using the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Restrict a cocone on $p\mapsto C_p$ to the objects $L(j)$ of Step 3. This is a cocone on $J(B)$, and the morphism $L(S(p))\to p$ with components $(1,v_p)$ shows that its value at $S(p)$ is the original leg at $p$. Conversely pull back a cocone on $J(B)$ along $S$; these operations are inverse since $SL=1$. Thus the maps $c_p:C_p\to B$ exhibit $B$ as the source colimit. For targets, let $(\lambda_p:D_p\to M)$ be a cocone and set $\mu_{j'}=\lambda_{R(j')}$. For $b:j'\to j'_1$, compatibility with $R(b)$ gives $\mu_{j'_1}b=\mu_{j'}$, so this is a cocone on $J(B')$. Conversely a cocone $(\mu_{j'})$ on $J(B')$ gives $\lambda_p=\mu_{T(p)}$. Restricting this along $R$ returns $\mu$ since $TR=1$. Starting with $\lambda$, the morphism $R(T(p))\to p$ with components $(0,1_{D_p})$ gives $\lambda_{R(T(p))}=\lambda_p$, so the other composite returns $\lambda$. Both operations preserve maps of cocones. The universal property of $B'$ therefore exhibits it as the target colimit with legs $d_p$. The equations $d_pv_p=fc_p$ say the induced colimit morphism is exactly $f$, by uniqueness on all legs $c_p$. Equivalently, a cocone of arrows is a pair of component cocones whose vertex arrow commutes with them, so these two universal properties also give $f=\varinjlim_{P_f}v$ in the arrow category.

source.place: Final paragraph, first sentence: recover both vertices and the arrow from the canonical presentations

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-arrow-exact-colimits to the essentially small filtered square category, transporting exactness from its small model. The mapped canonical arrow cocones under ker and coker are colimits. Their diagrams consist of constructible objects by det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure. ObjectProperty.of_essentiallySmall_index reindexes each specified colimit presentation over the small model and proves ind-constructibility directly from its definition.

source.place: Final paragraph: commute the filtered colimit with kernels/cokernels and apply the definition of ind-constructibility

proof_origin.place: Six-step argument implemented by explicit projection finality, comma finite colimits, canonical presentations and the generic exact-colimit lemma.
